description: Create a one-time or recurring maintenance window that silences alerts for some or all monitors. While a window is in effect its monitors keep being checked, but no incident opens and no alert goes out. Use it around a deploy or reboot instead of pause_monitor; it does not cover heartbeats (use pause_heartbeat). For a recurring schedule run preview_maintenance_window first. Requires a key with the write scope. The plan caps how many windows exist (403 past it or when the plan has none; see max_maintenance_windows in get_plan_usage). An invalid argument or schedule is a 422 naming it. Returns the window. Example: {"name": "Deploy", "scope": "MONITOR", "monitor_ids": ["<id from list_monitors>"], "dtstart": "2026-10-14T22:00:00", "duration_minutes": 30}

dtstart.description: The first start, an ISO 8601 date-time in the wall-clock time of timezone, for example 2026-10-14T22:00:00. A UTC offset or Z is a 422.

duration_minutes.description: How long each occurrence lasts, 1 to 40320 minutes.

enabled.description: Default true; false stores the window without effect.

monitor_ids.description: Monitor uuids from list_monitors, at least one when scope is MONITOR. An id that is not a monitor of this organization is a 404.

rrule.description: Repeats the window: one iCal RRULE without the RRULE: prefix, at most 1024 characters, for example FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU;BYHOUR=3. Hourly, minutely and secondly frequencies are refused. Omit it for a one-time window.

scope.description: ORG covers every monitor of the organization and ignores monitor_ids; MONITOR covers only monitor_ids.

timezone.description: IANA zone name such as Europe/Berlin, at most 64 characters. The schedule repeats in it, so a weekly 03:00 stays 03:00 across daylight-saving changes. Defaults to the organization's timezone.

name: create_maintenance_window
title: Create a maintenance window
